newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-SMITH RELIEVED AS AUSTRALIA BEAT SPRINGBOKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMITH RELIEVED AS AUSTRALIA BEAT SPRINGBOKS.

text.p: Australia revived their Tri-Nations campaign and cheered besieged coach Greg Smith with a resounding 32-20 win over South Africa on Saturday.
One week after being outplayed 33-18 by New Zealand, Australia proved too committed and inventive for the World Cup holders, scoring four tries to three and fully deserving the win.
Veteran fly-half David Knox, a player previously written off this season by Smith as a defensive liability, turned around Australia's fortunes on his test recall.
Smith, whose future was in doubt after a bout of intense media criticism over his tactics and inconsistent team selection this season, praised his side's attitude.
"It doesn't really matter about me, I'm not that important," he said. "Everyone can see the Australian team has a lot of passion and pride in themselves."
Smith recalled Knox from a playing stint with South African province Natal as a replacement for injured Tim Horan, who has struggled at fly-half since being switched from centre this season.

Knox invigorated an Australian backline in which winger Ben Tune excelled with two tries and the fly-half proved a capable goalkicker in the absence of injured full-back Matt Burke, landing three conversions and two penalties.
But the Wallabies benefited from some feeble and half-hearted Springbok defence in scoring four first half tries.

"We gave a bad performance in terms of first time tackling," said South Africa coach Carel du Plessis. "Australia played with a lot of motivation but as a team we are not happy with that performance."
Knox set up the opening try for full-back and ACT Brumbies team mate Stephen Larkham in the eighth minute with a well-timed pass near the corner.
Man-of-the-match Tune also benefited from Knox's vision and quick delivery, scoring his two tries at the end of intricate moves in the 19th and 40th minutes.
In between, number eight Daniel Manu charged through more poor Springbok defending to score under the posts.

South Africa's lone reply before half-time resulted from an Australian lack of discipline when backchat by scrum-half George Gregan caused a home penalty to be reversed five metres from the Australian line.
Prop Os du Randt collected a short pass from the tap start and barged over from close range. Fly-half Jannie de Beer, who earlier kicked a penalty, landed the conversion.
In the final 20 minutes, South Africa added some respectability to the scoreline with consolation tries from lock Mark Andrews and De Beer.

The Australian pack, which has undergone repeated changes this season, provided a sufficiently strong platform going forward, with recalled lock Owen Finegan earning praise from Smith, and captain John Eales dominating the line-out.
Smith's position will be reviewed at the end of the Tri-Nations series, leaving open the possibility of a change before the tour to Argentina and Britain later in the year.

For South Africa, who have now followed a home series loss to the British Lions with two successive Tri-Nations defeats, next week's daunting trip to New Zealand offers little hope of a change of fortunes.
The All Blacks lead the southern hemisphere competition with nine points from two games, four points clear of Australia. South Africa prop up the table with one point.
Teams:

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Daniel Manu (22-Troy Coker, 56), 7-David Wilson, 6-Matt Cockbain (19-Brett Robinson 58), 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Owen Finegan, 3-Andrew Heath (20-Andrew Blades, 71), 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw; 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Otto, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt (20-Adrian Garvey, 61).
